## Before We Start

**Definition:** 

An application programming interface (API) is a connection between computers or between computer programs. A type of software interface.

**Materials:**

Slides and code at [pricele2.github.io/blog](https://pricele2.github.io/blog.html)  

Plain text API key registered to Baker Ripley

## Federal Responsibility  

::: r-fit-text
Constitution requires a headcount of *all persons* every 10 years

- Article 1 Section 2: US House seats

- 1790: First national count 

- 1902: Permanent agency  

Present-Day:

- Within the Department of Commerce  

- Over 4,000 employees
:::

## Contains Multitudes

Sometimes mundane, sometimes controversial  

- Slavery, citizenship

- Movement between places  

- Indigenous Peoples and LGBTQ+ civil rights  

- Equitable representation    

- Door-to-door "enumeration" for Decennial

- Statistical "fuzzing" through noise injection 

## Diverse Data, Many Purposes

Over 130 different surveys ("data products")

Each has its own life cycle and its own characteristics

Drives annual distribution of **more than \$675 billion** in federal funds to local, state, and tribal governments

## Three Data Products

**Decennial Census of Population and Housing (10-Year).** 

- As required by US constitution, used for redistricting  

**American Community Survey (Annual).** 

- The social and economic needs of communities, across many demographic characteristics  

**Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (Annual).** 

- Income and poverty statistics for all school districts, counties, and states

## Geographies Start with Blocks

[![Census geographies are built from Blocks, aggregated to Counties to States](/images/census-work/census-geo-levels.jpg){fig-alt="Hierarchy of US Census geographies, with Nation at the top and Blocks at the very bottom" fig-align="center" width="757"}](https://www2.census.gov/geo/pdfs/reference/geodiagram.pdf)

## Our Census Location, Mapped

Let's look up the [Census Geographies for Baker Ripley Central](https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/geographies/onelineaddress?address=4450%20Harrisburg%20Blvd%2C%20Houston%2C%20Texas&benchmark=4&vintage=4)

**GEOID:** Unique ID for each census block, 15 digits. **48 201 310400 3032**

![4450 Harrisburg Blvd](/images/census-work/block-group-tract-BR.jpg){fig-alt="Greyscale line map from data.census.gov showing a highlighted section of city blocks" fig-align="left" width="685"}

## Blocks, Groups, Tracts

::: r-fit-text
**FIPS:** Five-digit code for each state (**48 Texas**) and county (**201 Harris**).

**Tract:** Smaller than a county: think *neighborhood*. Contains block groups. 

- Ideally contain about 4,000 people and 1,600 housing units.   

- Harris County has 1,115 Census tracts (2020 DHC) 
<!-- # Tract 310400 -->

**Block Group:** A subdivision of a census tract. Contains blocks.

- Generally between 600 — 3,000 people and 240 — 1,200 housing units.  

- Smallest unit for which the Bureau tabulates data for *any survey other than Decennial*. 
- Harris County has 2,830 block groups
<!-- - **Block Groups 1, 2, and 3** -->

**Block:** The smallest unit for which the Bureau tabulates *decennial* census data.  

- In cities, many blocks correspond to individual city blocks bounded by streets.   

- Harris County has 51,077 Census blocks
<!-- - **Block 3032**  -->
:::

## Let's start
```{r}
#| label: install.library
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: false
# Do this extra step the first time
# install.packages(c("tidycensus", "tidygeocoder", "censusapi", "tidyverse", "mapview"))

library(tidycensus)
library(tidyverse) # dplyr and ggplot2
library(mapview)
library(censusapi)
library(tidygeocoder)
library(sf)

# Check if you already have a CENSUS_KEY or CENSUS_API_KEY saved
get_api_key() 

# If your key returns, no further action is needed
```

## Set Up Census API Key
```{r}
#| label: set.api.key
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: false
# If not, use the functions you've already loaded 

# To add your key to your R environment file
census_api_key("PASTEYOURKEYHERE", overwrite = FALSE, install = TRUE)

# Reload .Renviron and check again
readRenviron("~/.Renviron")

# Confirm that the expected key prints to Console
get_api_key() 
```
Applause!!!

## Redistricting Dataset (PL)

Smaller dataset produced from DHC for redistricting under Public Law 94-171 (PL)

The summary file tables include:

P1. – Race  

P2. – Hispanic or Latino, and not Hispanic or Latino by Race  

P3. – Race for the Population 18 Years and Over  

P4. – Hispanic or Latino, by Race for the Population 18 Years and Over  

P5. – Group Quarters Population by Major Group Quarters Type  

H1. – Occupancy Status (Housing)  

## **P1_001N** : Total Pop from DHC

Let's use the script! 

By default, `get_decennial()` sets the arguments year = 2020 and sumfile = "pl". 

The `county` field accepts a string or FIPS code ("201"). 

Try "Harris" first. 

```{r}
#| label: harris.blocks
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: false

harris_pop_2020 = get_decennial(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = "P1_001N", # TOTAL POPULATION
  state = "TX",
  county = "Harris County", 
  sumfile = "pl", 
  year = 2020, 
  geometry = FALSE, 
  show_call = TRUE) 
```

## Harris County, 2020

Number of units in the geography

```{r}
#| echo: true
length(unique(harris_pop_2020$GEOID))
```

And here is our total population: 
```{r}
#| echo: true
h_pop = harris_pop_2020 |> 
  group_by(variable) |> 
  summarise(pop = sum(value))

print(h_pop[1,])
```
What happens when you swap in `year = 2010`?

## **P001001** : Population from PL 2010

Different variable name for `Total Population`! 
```{r}
#| label: harris2010
#| echo: true
#| eval: true
vars_pl_2010 = load_variables(2010, "pl") # Let's look for it

harris_pop_2010 = get_decennial(
  geography = "tract",
  # variables = "P1_001N", # Varname from 2020 
  variables = "P001001",
  state = "TX",
  county = "Harris County", 
  sumfile = "pl", 
  year = 2010, 
  geometry = FALSE, 
  show_call = TRUE)

h_pop_2010 = harris_pop_2010 |>

```

## Try Housing Occupancy, by County 
Here, using the DHC file and variable names
```{r}
#| label: housing.map
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: false

## 13 Counties served by Workforce Solutions
gulf_housing_2020 = get_decennial(
    geography = "county", 
    variables = c("H3_002N", "H3_003N"), # Occupied, Vacant
    summary_var = "H3_001N", # total Housing Units
    state = "TX", 
    county = ws_gulf_coast,
    sumfile = "dhc", 
    year = 2020, geometry = TRUE, # Changed from FALSE
    show_call = TRUE) |> 
  mutate(pct = 100 * (value /  summary_value)) 
```
Once we have the datset, we plot in the next step: 
```{r}
#| label: housing.map2
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true
#| output-location: slide
# Note: the mutate / value / summary syntax here is specific to tidycensus
# Otherwise would require a group_by() summarize() situation

ggplot(gulf_housing_2020, aes(fill = pct, color = pct)) + 
  geom_sf() + 
  facet_wrap(~ variable)
```

## Let's Clean Up The Map
```{r}
#| label: housing.map3
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true

gulf_counties2 = gulf_housing_2020 |> 
  rename(summary_value, "Housing Units" = summary_value) |>
  mutate(housing_status =
    case_when(
      variable == "H3_002N" ~ "Occupied", 
      variable == "H3_003N" ~ "Vacant"
    )) |> 
  select(-variable)
```
Rename items, and then reverse-code the fill and color
```{r}
#| label: housing.map4
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true
#| output-location: slide

ggplot(gulf_counties2, 
       aes(fill = -pct, color = -pct)) + 
  geom_sf() + 
  facet_wrap(~ housing_status)
```

## ACS and Population Changes

**American Community Survey (Annual).** The social and economic needs of communities, across many demographic characteristics. 

Language spoken at home, education, commuting, employment, mortgage/rent status, income, poverty and health insurance coverage. 

[Subjects in the ACS](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/guidance/subjects.html)

[Five Year vs One Year Estimates](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/guidance/estimates.html) 

<!-- [Which Data Tool or Table Should I Use?](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/guidance/which-data-tool.html) -->

## Tradeoffs: Recency and Precision  

The ACS is the only source of local statistics for most of the 40-plus topics it covers.

- `tidycensus::get_acs()` also handles ZIP or ZCTRA inputs  

- `censusapi::getCensus()` will retrieve from any API with its programmatic name 

## SAIPE and Children

**Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates (Annual).** 
Income and poverty statistics for all school districts, counties, and states.

- Not included in `tidycensus` functionality  

- Is included in `censusapi` toolkit, through `getCensus()`  

  `"timeseries/poverty/saipe"`  # States and Counties, through 2024
  
  `"timeseries/poverty/saipe/schdist"` # Districts, through 2024

## What data elements and time points are in each API? 

Metadata to the rescue! `listCensusMetadata` 

Critical argument is `type`: 

- "geographies", or "groups", or "variables" (use include_values = TRUE) 

- Confirm that Block-Level is for the Decennial (PL or DHC) survey only 

```{r}
vars_acs5 = listCensusMetadata(
  name = "acs/acs5",
  vintage = 2024,
  key = NULL,
  type = "variables",
  # group = NULL,
  # variable_name = NULL,
  # include_values = FALSE
)
```

## Geocode One Location for ACS

[Find Geographies for One Address](https://geocoding.geo.census.gov/geocoder/geographies/onelineaddress?form) 

- State, County, Tract, Block Group  

## Batch geocode with `tidygeocoder::geo()`

The geocode function utilizes this function on addresses contained in dataframes. 

Let's do it! 

```{r}
#| label: geocode.one
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true

library(sf)
baker_r <- geo("4450 Harrisburg Blvd, Houston TX") 

baker_r_sf <- st_as_sf(baker_r, coords = c("long", "lat"),
                   crs = 4326) # Coord Reference System

br_5km <- baker_r_sf %>%
  st_buffer(5000)

mapview(br_5km) + mapview(baker_r_sf)
```

Since now we have an input area representing the 5 kilometers around the address, we can pass this as the `filter_by` argument in `get_decennial()` or `get_acs()`. 

This gives back the Census blocks within 5km of the address without any additional need for spatial overlay.

```{r}
#| label: pull.blockpop.dhc
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true

block_pop_brc <- get_decennial(
  geography = "block",
  variables = "P1_001N",
  state = "TX",
  county = "Harris County",
  geometry = TRUE,
  filter_by = br_5km,
  sumfile = "dhc",
  year = 2020
) 

mapview(block_pop_brc)

sum(block_pop_brc$value) 
```

## Now let's try all BR Sites! 

```{r}
#| label: geocode.brsites
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true

all_hs = read_csv("~/R/pricele2.github.io/blog/census-workshop/data/all_ehs_hs_tx_locations.csv") |> as_tibble() |> 
  rename(Add1 = 6) # |> mutate(Mail_Address = str_c(Add1, Add2, sep = " "))

colnames(all_hs)

hs_geos = geocode(  # Note the full word for the full dataset 
  all_hs, 
  # street = "Mail_Address",
  street = "Add1",
  city = "city",
  state = "state",
  postalcode = "zip",
  method = "census",
  full_results = TRUE,
  api_options = list(census_return_type = "geographies")
)

colSums(is.na(hs_geos)) #152 missing, probably need data cleaning

hs_geos2 = hs_geos |> 
  filter(state_fips == "48") #drops the rows with "NA" returned
  
hs_geos_sf = st_as_sf(hs_geos2, 
      coords = c("long", "lat"),
      crs = 4326) |> 
  filter(county_fips %in% ws_gulf_coast) 
  
hs_all_5km <- hs_geos_sf |> 
  st_buffer(5000) 

mapview(hs_all_5km) + mapview(hs_geos_sf)

```

```{r}
#| label: pull.blockpop.acs5
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
#| code-overflow: wrap
#| output: true

vars_acs = load_variables(2024, "acs5") # Searched for "Under 5"

block_pop_wsgc_u5_pov <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = c("B17001_004", "B17001_018"), 
  year = 2024, # Defaults to 2023 
  state = "TX",
  # filter_by = hs_all_5km,
  geometry = TRUE
  )  

str_length(block_pop_wsgc_u5_pov$GEOID[1]) # 11

sum(block_pop_wsgc_u5_pov$estimate) # 388,508 across Texas
```
